claim: For every finite quiver \(Q\) (loops and parallel arrows allowed) and every finite field \(\mathbb F_q\), let \(A=\mathbb F_q Q/J^2\), where \(J\) is the arrow ideal. Let \(\mathcal S(Q)\) be the arrow subsets containing no composable pair; for \(S\in\mathcal S(Q)\), let \(c(S)\) be the component count of its underlying undirected multigraph on all vertices and put \(\beta(S)=|S|-|Q_0|+c(S)\). Then the isomorphism classes of \(A\)-modules with dimension vector \(\mathbf 1\), refined by endomorphism-algebra dimension, are enumerated by \(\mathcal P_Q(q,z)=\sum_{S\in\mathcal S(Q)}(q-1)^{\beta(S)}z^{c(S)}\); every module in the \(S\)-stratum has \(\operatorname{End}_A(M)\cong\mathbb F_q^{c(S)}\) and \(|\operatorname{Aut}_A(M)|=(q-1)^{c(S)}\).
integrity: The general claim follows from the explicit support and torus-orbit proof. The included finite checker is corroborative only and is not used as an infinite proof.
scientific_limitations: Only modules with dimension vector one at every vertex over finite fields for the square-zero arrow ideal; no higher dimension vectors or higher radical powers. The proof is exact, but originality is provisional because an equivalent support-graph formula may exist in older literature.
title: Thin modules over radical-square-zero quiver algebras: a support-graph enumerator
